backgroundVow.title: Chart a route through the Forge that no institution's maps dare claim, proving the stars can be trusted more than any authority.
backgroundVow.reason: Reflects her rejection of duty to institutions and her drive to prove her own charts superior, a personal but demanding quest.

hooks.text: Dash fled a bounty hunter guild's rigid chain of command after refusing an unjust order, and still watches her back for their reach.
hooks.reason: Grounds the escape from an abusive/unjust situation in the setting's bounty hunter guild truth.

hooks.text: She was groomed to captain one of the Ironhomes, a legacy vessel of the Exodus, but walked away from that inherited destiny to fly free.
hooks.reason: Ties the rejected duty or destiny to the Ironhomes truth, explaining her distrust of institutions.

hooks.text: Dash keeps her own hand-drawn charts, refusing to rely on hoarded, jealously-guarded institutional data.
hooks.reason: Connects her navigator concept and distrust of institutions to the setting's truth about hoarded information.

appearance.value: What people notice first is the way her eyes flick constantly to instruments and horizon alike, as if she's always plotting the next course.

backstory.text: Ash Valk was raised aboard one of the Ironhomes, the great Exodus vessels that never truly landed, groomed from childhood to one day captain it and carry on its insular traditions. But she chafed against the ship's rigid hierarchy and the guild contracts it enforced on its crew, including a stint working bounty runs for a guild whose leadership demanded she hunt a debtor she believed innocent. When she refused, the guild turned on her, and she fled in a stolen skiff with nothing but her own hand-drawn charts and a stubborn belief that the stars owed her no institution's permission to follow them. She never went back to the Ironhome, and never took up the captaincy that was meant to be hers. Now she flies free, trusting the paths she's charted herself over any authority's word.
backstory.reason: Combines both backstory prompts with the setting's Exodus, Ironhomes, and bounty hunter guild truths to explain her distrust of institutions.

signatureGear.value: A worn satchel of hand-drawn star charts, annotated and corrected over years of travel.
signatureGear.reason: A navigator who trusts her own charts over institutional data would carry this as a prized, practical possession.

callsign.reason: The oracle's callsign fits an engineer whose hands are always tinkering, tightening, adjusting.

name.reason: Direct use of the rolled name, evoking the Exodus-shard traditions of the setting.

appearance.value: A blunt, patchwork hull of mismatched plating and scavenged armor, welded together in a way that looks more like a grave marker than a ship—fitting, since half her bones came from someone else's wreck. Faint rust-brown stains ghost through the airlock paint no matter how many times it's redone.
appearance.reason: Draws on the derelict-and-patched history and the recurring bloodstain quirk to give a visceral first impression.

history.value: The Iron Cairn was found drifting and gutted, an old hulk stripped of crew and purpose, and the three of them spent months welding her back into something spaceworthy. Some of her original systems still hum beneath the patched plating, remnants of whoever built her first and never got to fly her home.
history.reason: Built directly from the rolled history of being discovered derelict and repaired.

quirks.value: No matter how many times the airlock is repainted, a dark stain seeps back through in the same spot, like the ship remembers something the crew doesn't.
quirks.reason: Direct dramatization of the rolled quirk about the reappearing bloodstain.

quirks.value: Several deck plates throughout the ship pop free to reveal hidden storage compartments, clearly added by a previous owner for reasons never explained.
quirks.reason: Direct dramatization of the rolled quirk about hidden storage under removable decking.

output.reason: The ship's rolled name, salvage-and-repair origin, and unsettling quirks reinforce the Forge's scarcity and superstition while giving the crew a haunted, hand-me-down home that suits Vesna's distrust of official charts and Juno's mechanical eye.

segments.text: Vesna lays her hand against the beacon receiver's cold housing and swears aloud to find the recorder of Meridian's Hope.
The beacon's old relay lights flicker in response, a faint hum rising through the anchorage's patched plating as if the station itself takes note of the vow.
A steadiness settles through her, momentum gathering like current finding a clear channel.

Segment 2's sensation of steadiness/momentum follows directly from the resolved effect (+2 momentum) and is permissible.

segments.text: The beacon at Deepwater Anchorage hums low beneath the lattice of cabling, its receiver housing scarred with old solder and salt-white corrosion.
Vesna lays her hand on the beacon receiver and swears to find the recorder.
Something in the connection catches, a faint answering pulse traveling up through the metal into her palm, steady and sure.
The beacon's indicator light steadies from a flickering amber to a solid, patient green, as if the old machine itself has taken note of the promise made against it.
